item.title: Pentagon seeks help from Ford and GM | Honolulu Star-Advertiser
item.description: The Pentagon has met with senior executives of Ford Motor and General Motors to gauge whether the auto industry could help the military acquire vehicles, munitions or other hardware more quickly and at lower costs, according to three people familiar with the talks.

item.title: Kaiser says contracts with all Alliance union members ratified | Honolulu Star-Advertiser
item.description: Kaiser Permanente announced today that after nearly 11 months of negotiations, more than 52 collective bargaining agreements have now been ratified for union employees.

item.title: Woman, 53, arrested on suspicion of attempted murder in Wahiawa stabbing | Honolulu Star-Advertiser
item.description: A 47-year-old woman suffered serious injuries after a stabbing in Wahiawa this morning, and police arrested a 53-year-old woman on suspicion of attempted murder.

item.title: American Airlines says it won’t merge with United | Honolulu Star-Advertiser
item.description: American Airlines today dismissed the idea of merging with United Airlines, saying in a statement that a combination of the two industry giants would be “negative for competition and for consumers.”

item.title: HPD officer fired at ‘dangerous dog’ in Waimanalo; dog was not injured | Honolulu Star-Advertiser
item.description: The Honolulu Police Department said that an officer shot at a dog multiple times in Waimanalo this morning while responding to a call, but that it managed to run away, and appeared to be uninjured.

item.title: Market-rate condo sales free up less-expensive housing | Honolulu Star-Advertiser
item.description: Most island families can never afford a newly built home, but those who bought condos in the five-year-old building near Ala Moana Center called The Century opened up lower-priced housing behind them as they moved up Hawaii’s housing ladder, according to a report released Monday by the University of Hawaii Economic Research Organization.

item.title: Emotions run high at military land-lease event in Waikiki | Honolulu Star-Advertiser
item.description: Military officials and community members gathered Monday at the Ala Moana Hotel for a discussion of military land leases and their future in Hawaii. Almost immediately, the conversation became heated and at times emotional.

item.title: Waiau power plant Biofuel project approved | Honolulu Star-Advertiser
item.description: The state Public Utilities Commission has snubbed a request by the state’s chief energy officer to defer a decision on a proposed biofuel power plant on Oahu, approving the project Monday.

item.title: State asserts LNG study accurate despite error | Honolulu Star-Advertiser
item.description: After admitting a spreadsheet error inflated the benefits of liquefied natural gas, or LNG, by hundreds of millions of dollars in at least one scenario in an alternative fuels study, the Hawaii State Energy Office said another scenario still shows cost savings.

item.title: Sakanoko leads UH’s Big West awards haul | Honolulu Star-Advertiser
item.description: Louis Sakanoko cramped up so bad in Friday’s five-set win over Long Beach State, he had to sub out in the third set and didn’t come back.

item.title: FCC bans new foreign router imports over security risks | Honolulu Star-Advertiser
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission said on Monday it was banning the import of all new foreign-made consumer routers, the latest crackdown on Chinese-made electronic gear over security concerns.

item.title: Markwayne Mullin confirmed as homeland security secretary | Honolulu Star-Advertiser
item.description: WASHINGTON &gt;&gt; The Senate confirmed Markwayne Mullin as homeland security secretary on Monday, installing a Trump loyalist to head the agency responsible for carrying out immigration enforcement at a time when it is reeling from dimming public opinion.

item.title: China builds vast seabed map to boost submarine warfare capability | Honolulu Star-Advertiser
item.description: SYDNEY &gt;&gt; China is conducting a vast undersea mapping and monitoring operation across the Pacific, Indian and Arctic oceans, building detailed knowledge of marine conditions that naval experts say would be crucial for waging submarine warfare against the United States and its allies.
